data.name: Sharveshwara
data.gender_notes: Sharveshwara is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The one who holds the universe in his form, a manifestation of Lord Shiva. The name Sharveshwara carries the meaning “Lord of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sharveshwara usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of cosmic consciousness and the supreme being
data.etymology: Sharveshwara belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharveshwara total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Sharveshwara" is a revered and significant one in Hindu culture, representing Lord Shiva in his aspect as the one who holds the universe in his form. This name is often used to denote the supreme power, the all-pervading existence, and the ultimate reality beyond the material world. Sarveshwara is also a central deity in various temples and religious practices across India and beyond, symbolizing the unity, interconnectedness, and infinite nature of the cosmos.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the name "Sharveshwara" holds deep spiritual significance, as it signifies the ultimate reality and the source of all existence. It is believed that Lord Shiva, in his aspect as Sarveshwara, represents the pure consciousness that underlies all matter and the eternal self that dwells within every being. Therefore, invoking the name Sharveshwara is seen as a means to connect with this divine consciousness and attain spiritual growth, self-realization, and ultimate liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Sharveshwara signifies the embodiment of supreme consciousness and absolute wisdom. It represents the presence of Shiva, the destroyer, in its most enlightened form, transcending time and space.

historical_references.reference: Sharveshwara is a form of Shiva, particularly revered in the southern Indian states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. This name is associated with the Natha tradition and the cult of the Shaiva saints, which flourished between the 11th and 16th centuries.
historical_references.context: The Natha tradition was a syncretic movement that incorporated elements of Buddhism, Jainism, and Shaivism. The Shaiva saints, also known as the Aghoras, were known for their unconventional practices, including the consumption of human flesh and cremated remains. Sharveshwara was one of the many forms of Shiva worshipped by these saints.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Sharveshwara can be found in the Kannada literature of the medieval period. The poet-saint Allama Prabhu (15th century) wrote extensively about Sharveshwara in his work 'Vijayamitra'. He describes Sharveshwara as a form of Shiva that removes all obstacles and bestows blessings upon his devotees.
historical_references.context: Allama Prabhu was a prominent figure in the Kannada literary tradition, and his works continue to be studied and revered in Karnataka today. In his poetry, he explores various aspects of Shaiva theology, and Sharveshwara is one of the many forms of Shiva that he discusses.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Sharveshwara' is a revered name in Hinduism, referring to Lord Shiva as the protector and preserver. In modern contexts, this name is seen on various digital platforms. On Google Maps, users can search for places dedicated to Lord Sharveshwara, such as temples and shrines, and plan their religious tourism accordingly. Airbnb listings often include properties named 'Sharveshwara Temple Stay', offering tourists an authentic Hindu experience. Lastly, on Instagram, there is a popular trend of users posting pictures of Lord Sharveshwara idols or temples, often using the hashtag #Sharveshwara, alongside spiritual or inspirational captions.
